name: Brandon Oberdorfer
intro: Brandon leads the team and runs the part of every move that happens on paper: pricing, offers, negotiation and the long middle between an accepted offer and the closing table.
bio: Brandon started The Oberdorfer Team with Kait on a simple premise: people should be able to reach the person handling their move, and that person should know the ground. He holds a Massachusetts broker license and spends most of his week either walking houses or on the phone with lenders, attorneys and other agents keeping deals on track.

He is most useful when the stakes feel high: a first offer in a competitive month, a sale that has to line up with a purchase, an inspection report that needs a calm read. Clients describe him the way you'd describe a good contractor: he tells you what it will take, then does it.
Outside of work you'll find him on the rail trail, at a WooSox game, or arguing about the best breakfast spot on Route 9.
bioStatus: Draft bio written for the concept — to be rewritten with Brandon.

portrait.direction: Brandon on the front walk of a listing, mid-sentence, turned three-quarters toward someone off-frame; overcast October light; 85mm, waist up.

quote: Most of this job is telling people the truth early, while it's still useful.

name: Kait Oberdorfer
intro: Kait is the team's guide to places. She plans tours, knows which streets flood and which ones have the good sidewalks, and writes most of the Field Guide.
bio: Kait co-founded The Oberdorfer Team and runs how the team works with people from the first conversation on. She plans showing days so they make sense on a map, prepares sellers' homes for photographs, and keeps notes on towns the way other people keep recipes.

Her favorite clients are the ones who aren't sure yet. She'll spend an afternoon driving three towns with someone relocating from out of state, then send a page of notes on what they saw: where the town center is, what the houses on the side streets look like, how long the drive to Worcester really took at 8 a.m.
She writes the team's Field Guide and is responsible for most of its opinions about coffee.
bioStatus: Draft bio written for the concept — role, licensing and bio to be confirmed with Kait.

portrait.direction: Kait at a kitchen island with a notebook open, a client's hands in the foreground; window light from the left; 50mm, eye level, unposed.

quote: A town makes sense once you've seen where people actually go on a Saturday.

name: Jane Smith
intro: Example profile. This page shows how a new team member appears once they're added in the CMS — same system, their own voice.
bio: This is a sample agent profile created to demonstrate how the site grows. When a new agent joins, the team adds a single Agent entry in WordPress — name, portrait, areas, specialties, contact details — and this page, their row in the team directory, their listings and their articles are assembled automatically.
Leads that start on this page are attributed to Jane and routed by the team's rules: to Jane directly, to a team lead, or to whoever is on call that day.

portrait.direction: Jane on a front porch steps with a tablet showing a floor plan, looking out at the street; late afternoon; 50mm.

quote: Example quote: the profile system supports a short line in the agent's own words.
